subject: Egress telemetry and allowlist onboarding for Crestview private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Reyes <security@crestviewhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya S. <ops@crestviewhealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-15T09:31:00Z
Subject: Private runtime allowlist / telemetry for SOC2 evidence - Crestview

Hi Marissa,

We're starting the security onboarding for the Crestview private deployment and need to lock down egress/firewall and telemetry requirements for our audit team. Specifically we need:

- A definitive list of outbound IP addresses and FQDNs (control plane, metrics & logs ingestion, model hub) to allowlist.
- Ports and protocols (TCP/443, additional ports if any).
- TLS-based identifiers we can collect (SNI hostnames, client certificate CNs, ocsp/tls fingerprints) for flow correlation.
- Guidance on NAT/fallback behavior if Redwood uses ephemeral egress addresses or regional fallbacks.
- A sample runbook snippet for firewall engineers showing minimal ACL lines and expected observable traffic.

Can you share the above along with any attachments we should include in the SOC2 packet? We're on a compressed timeline and need an initial bundle by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Alex Reyes
Security Engineer, Crestview Health

Attachment: crestview-egress-requirements.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reyes <security@crestviewhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-15T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private runtime allowlist / telemetry for SOC2 evidence - Crestview

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. High level answers below; I'll work with Ops to provide the canonical IP list + runbook snippets and attach the telemetry matrix.

Summary (initial):
- Control plane endpoints: control.redwood-inference.net:443 (IP range documented, prefer FQDN allowlist with TLS SNI validation where possible).
- Telemetry/metrics ingestion: metrics.redwood-inference.net:443 and logs.ingest.redwood-inference.net:443.
- Ports/protocols: outbound TCP/443 only for control/metrics. If you enable the optional image fetcher for private runtime admin tasks we will call out 443 for those artifact endpoints as well. No non-HTTP ports required by default.
- TLS identifiers: we can provide stable SNI hostnames and the expected server cert issuer CN. For additional assurance Ops can capture TLS cert SHA256 fingerprints and SNI from TLS Client Hello.
- NAT/fallback: Redwood Private supports two modes — static egress IP blocks (recommended for strict allowlist), or regional ephemeral egress with hostname-based fallback. We'll provide explicit guidance for both.

I'm attaching an "egress-telemetry-matrix.xlsx" that maps each external hostname to the required telemetry signals (flow logs, SNI, cert fingerprint, proxy logs). We'll follow up with IPs and a runbook snippet from Ops.

Next steps: Vaness a / David — can you validate the IP set for the US-west region and paste a minimal firewall ACL snippet plus a short verification checklist we can hand to Crestview? Aim for a single CSV + 3-line ACL example.

Marissa
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: egress-telemetry-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-15T11:02:00Z
Subject: FW: Private runtime allowlist / telemetry for SOC2 evidence - Crestview

Vanessa, David — looping you in to get the authoritative IP list & ops runbook for Crestview. Key asks from Alex:

1) Canonical egress IP set (preferred: a static CIDR list we can provide to the customer). If we cannot provide static ranges for a mode, call out the recommended product configuration to enable static egress.
2) Minimal firewall ACL sample (ip/cidr/port/proto) we can paste in their ticket.
3) A short verification checklist (how they validate traffic is reaching metrics/logs endpoints during onboarding) — include curl/tcpdump examples and the SNI/cert handshake checks.
4) Any MTLS or client-cert requirements for private management plane (I believe we support mutual TLS for the control plane in Private deployments; confirm).

Please reply with the CSV + one short pasted runbook snippet today.

Thanks — Marissa

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Marissa / Vanessa — see the canonical items below for US-west Private running in static-egress mode. I've included a tiny runbook and the CSV attachment (egress-ip-set.csv) in case you want to hand it off.

Canonical egress (US-west static):
- 34.201.16.0/22 (control plane, TLS SNI: control.redwood-inference.net)
- 18.204.32.0/23 (metrics/logs ingestion, TLS SNI: metrics.redwood-inference.net, logs.ingest.redwood-inference.net)
- 52.12.48.0/24 (artifact pulls / optional admin agent)

Ports/protocols: Allow outbound TCP/443 to the above CIDRs. No additional ports required.

Runbook snippet (to paste into customer ticket):
1) Add outbound ACL entries:
   - allow tcp any 34.201.16.0/22 eq 443
   - allow tcp any 18.204.32.0/23 eq 443
   - allow tcp any 52.12.48.0/24 eq 443
2) Validation (customer):
   - From a private runtime host run: curl -vkI https://control.redwood-inference.net/healthz --resolve control.redwood-inference.net:443:34.201.16.10
   - Confirm TLS SNI in proxy logs or use tshark filter: tls.handshake.extensions_server_name == "control.redwood-inference.net"
   - Verify server cert issuer matches "Redwood Inference Ops CA" or check cert SHA256 fingerprint: 3f:1c:...:a2
3) Telemetry to capture for SOC2 evidence:
   - VPC flow logs (5-tuple) for flows to the CIDRs above.
   - Proxy access logs including request timestamp, client IP, destination SNI, and HTTP status.
   - TLS server cert fingerprint recorded at first connection (one-time hash) for correlation.

MTLS: For high-security deployments we require mutual TLS for the management/control plane. If Crestview elects mTLS we will provide a client cert bundle and CN values that should be permitted by the customer's proxy or firewall. If they prefer not to use mTLS, TLS with SNI + IP allowlist + proxy logging is acceptable for SOC2 scoping.

Attached: egress-ip-set.csv (CSV stub) — columns: cidr, purpose, sni, recommended_note

David Kim
Infrastructure/Edge Reliability | Redwood Inference
